_note: Teardown/breakdown data for the Showroom's exploded view. Anchors in FITTED car space (~3.4 units long, grounded y=0, +X nose, +Y up, +Z left). `materials` are GLB material-name substrings matched first-match-wins in this part order — the body's `CIVIC13` over-matches the suffixed wheel/interior/light materials, so those specific parts are listed BEFORE body to claim their meshes first. This GLB has real brake + wheel meshes but no engine mesh, and it's FWD like the FC3, so engine/drivetrain/suspension use the procedural stand-ins. Copy grounded on data/cars/43-honda-civic-si-9th.json; anchors from frontend/scripts/model_meshes.mjs.

parts.label: Four-Wheel Disc Brakes
parts.summary: Four-wheel discs sized for the Si — plenty of stopping power for a ~2,875 lb coupe.
parts.detail: Four-wheel discs sized for the Si — more than enough for a ~2,875 lb car, and an easy target for pads and fluid.
parts.watch: Pads and fluid are the only real upgrade for spirited or track use.

parts.label: 18" Wheels & Tires
parts.summary: Eighteen-inch alloys on grippy rubber — the footprint that works with the factory helical LSD.
parts.detail: Factory 18-inch alloys on performance tires — the setup that lets the helical limited-slip put the K24's fat midrange down.
parts.watch: Curb rash and pothole damage on the low-profile 18s; sticky summer tires wake the car up.

parts.label: Interior & Driver's Cockpit
parts.summary: The two-tier Si dash, bolstered seats, and the notchy short-throw six-speed.
parts.detail: The 9th-gen's two-tier digital/analog dash with the Si's bolstered sport seats and 6-speed shifter. The 2012 cars had hard-plastic trim; Honda improved it in the 2013 refresh.
parts.watch: The one real gripe is the cheap-feeling 2012 interior — prefer a 2013–2015 car. Feel for 3rd-gear synchro notchiness on a test drive.

parts.label: Lighting & Electronics
parts.summary: The Si's headlight and tail-lamp assemblies and its accessory electrics.
parts.detail: Halogen/projector head lamps and the Si's tail-lamp clusters, plus the era's i-MID display and Civic accessory systems.
parts.watch: Straightforward and durable; the early i-MID software is dated but reliable.

parts.label: Body, Aero & Glass
parts.summary: The steel unibody FG4 coupe — the sportier two-door of the 9th-gen Si pair.
parts.detail: Steel unibody as the FG4 coupe (the two-door for buyers who wanted the sportier body), around 2,875 lbs, with the Si's fascias and decklid spoiler.
parts.watch: Solid structure; watch for rock chips and parking dings like any daily-driven compact.

parts.label: 2.4L K24Z7 i-VTEC Engine
parts.summary: The biggest-displacement engine in Si history — a torquey 2.4-liter i-VTEC four.
parts.detail: 2.4L K24Z7 DOHC i-VTEC four — the biggest-displacement engine in Si history. 205 hp and 174 lb-ft (2014–2015) with a fat, usable midrange, and chain-driven (no timing belt). (Shown as a procedural stand-in — not a separate mesh in this model.)
parts.watch: Genuinely stout — the main K-series quirk is the harmless cold-start VTC actuator rattle. Keep the oil clean and it lasts.

parts.label: 6-Speed Manual & Helical LSD
parts.summary: A short-throw six-speed sending the K24's torque to the front wheels through a helical LSD.
parts.detail: 6-speed manual driving the front wheels through a helical limited-slip differential — carried over from the 8th gen and working beautifully with the K24's torque. (Procedural stand-in — not a separate mesh.)
parts.watch: 3rd-gear synchro wear shows up on hard-shifted cars — feel for notchiness. Inspect the clutch on any tuned car.

parts.label: Strut Front / Multi-Link Rear
parts.summary: MacPherson strut front and independent multi-link rear, sport-tuned for the Si.
parts.detail: MacPherson strut front and independent multi-link rear, evolved from the 8th-gen platform with sport tuning for a slightly more compliant balance. (Procedural stand-in — not a separate mesh.)
parts.watch: Bushings and dampers soften with miles; coilovers and sway bars are the usual upgrade to tighten it back up around the factory LSD.
